title: Environmental Chemistry: Air, Water, Climate

cards.b: Smog over Delhi in winter, the ozone hole, acid rain, polluted rivers, a warming climate: each is a chemistry problem, and each has a chemistry-led solution.

Troposphere (weather, up to about 10-15 km), stratosphere (ozone layer), then higher layers. Air is about 78 percent N2 and 21 percent O2. Pollutants alter the balance: CO, SO2, NOx, particulates (PM2.5 and PM10) and volatile organics.

Ozone (O3) in the stratosphere absorbs harmful UV-B light. Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) from fridges and sprays rise, UV splits off chlorine atoms, and each chlorine can destroy thousands of ozone molecules: Cl + O3 → ClO + O2. Mario Molina and F. Sherwood Rowland warned in 1974; the ozone hole over Antarctica was reported in 1985.

The Montreal Protocol (1987) phased out CFCs, among the most successful environmental treaties; ozone is recovering.

Gases such as CO2, CH4, N2O and water vapour absorb infrared heat radiated by Earth and re-emit it, keeping Earth about 33 °C warmer than it would be. Burning fossil fuels, C + O2 → CO2, adds more. CO2 rose from about 280 ppm before industry to above 420 ppm in the mid-2020s. Methane traps far more heat per molecule than CO2 over short periods.

Burning coal releases SO2, vehicles release NOx. In air: SO2 → H2SO4 and NO2 → HNO3, so rain pH falls below about 5.6 (normal rain is slightly acidic from CO2). It damages marble, soil and lakes.

Photochemical smog: sunlight, NOx and hydrocarbons make ozone and irritants at ground level. CO2 also dissolves in oceans: CO2 + H2O ⇌ H2CO3, acidifying seas and harming corals.

• Hardness: dissolved Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions.
  • BOD (biochemical oxygen demand): oxygen microbes need to digest waste. High BOD means polluted water.
  • Eutrophication: fertiliser nitrate and phosphate cause algae blooms that use up oxygen and kill fish.
  • Toxic contaminants: arsenic, fluoride, lead, pesticides.

Treatment: filtration, coagulation (alum), chlorination or UV disinfection.

C + O2 → CO2. 12 g carbon gives 44 g CO2. So 1 kg carbon gives 44/12 = 3.67 kg CO2.

Petrol (roughly C8H18): burning 1 litre releases about 2.3 kg of CO2, as most of the carbon in the fuel ends up as gas. A car using 5 L daily emits about 11.5 kg CO2 a day.

• The ozone hole is not the cause of global warming. They are different problems, though some CFCs are also greenhouse gases.
  • The greenhouse effect itself is natural and needed. The problem is enhancement.
  • Clear water is not necessarily safe (arsenic is invisible).
  • Acid rain is not melting people; it is mild but damaging over time.

India's Ganga Action Plan (1986) began sewage treatment to cut river pollution; Namami Gange followed in 2014. Groundwater arsenic affects the Gangetic plains in West Bengal and Bihar. The National Clean Air Programme (2019) targets reductions in PM2.5 and PM10 in polluted cities, and India has committed to net-zero emissions by 2070.

• CFCs destroy ozone; Montreal Protocol (1987) fixed it.
  • CO2, CH4, N2O trap heat; CO2 above 420 ppm.
  • SO2 and NOx make acid rain; fertiliser causes eutrophication.
  • 1 kg carbon burns to 3.67 kg CO2.
